_readme: Batch 26 data-rows spec. Every row is an absolute assignment for scripts/data/effect-backfill.json ({category,id,field,value}). ORDERING: rows marked "supersedes" REPLACE an existing row for the same category/id/field already in effect-backfill.json — the applier's last-write-wins means appending is not enough if the old row sorts after. Replace the old row in place.

backfillRows.value: Your ancestors have always had a connection to fire and a thicker skin, which allows you to resist burning. You gain fire resistance equal to half your level (minimum 1). You can also recover from being on fire more easily. findings.note: Print gives the HP unconditionally and the attribute swap as a separate 'you can choose to'. Three rows, all on ONE record. The alternateAttributes row SUPERSEDES the existing effect-backfill row for that field (same value minus `hp`) — it MUST replace it in place, not sit beside it, or hp:10 comes back and build.ts:8098 (`if (alt?.hp != null && c.ancestryHp === alt.hp) … = alt.whenChoice`) forces every mightyfall kobold's stored answer to 'kaiju' on decode. Engine agent 1 adjusts that decode; the choice-label row exists because '10 ancestry HP' stops being a property of the kaiju branch.

backfillRows.why: Print (heritage-374): 'You gain 10 Hit Points from your ancestry instead of 6.' — an unconditional clause, separate from the 'you can choose to' attribute sentence. Reader build.ts:696; stoutheart-centaur precedent.

SUPERSEDES the existing row. `hp` is dropped because print does not gate the 10 HP on the attribute package, and leaving it beside an unconditional ancestryHp:10 makes the decode at build.ts:8098 stamp every character's answer as 'kaiju'.

findings.note: RECORD side only. Both printed benefits move onto one effectChoices block: the banyan option carries EffectGrant.grantsFeats (batch-25 lane, read at build.ts:4647 with cataphract-fleshwarp as the precedent) and the fish option carries EffectGrant.speeds, folded into chosenEffects by mergeEffect (build.ts:5288) and consumed by deriveSpeeds at derive.ts:4746 — gnome has no swim on the chassis so 0+15 = 15. The record-level grantsFeats row DELETES the unconditional grant (it SUPERSEDES the existing effect-backfill grantsFeats row and must replace it in place, or the feat comes back for the fish branch). degreeShifts is left EXACTLY as it ships — gating the climb success-to-crit to the banyan branch is engine agent 2's half and needs a new answer gate on DegreeShift; I am not touching it.

You can catch any fish (swim Speed 15 feet)

backfillRows.why: Print (heritage-372): 'You gain your choice of the following benefits. Once made, this choice can't be changed.' Branch two (swim Speed 15) was unreachable and branch one was handed to everyone. Option-level grantsFeats is the cataphract-fleshwarp lane (build.ts:4647); option-level speeds reaches deriveSpeeds through chosenEffects (build.ts:5288 → derive.ts:4746).

SUPERSEDES the existing row. Print makes Combat Climber one BRANCH of a two-way choice; an unconditional record-level grant hands it to a player who chose the fish branch. The grant now lives on the banyan option.

findings.note: Reader: derive.ts:4761 `for (const h of heritageRecords(c, db)) featLandBonus += landBonusOf(h.landSpeedBonus)`, applied at derive.ts:4788 after the base; a negative number passes through landBonusOf unchanged. The `speeds` rewrite drops the inert `land: 0` — derive.ts:4726 gates heritage speeds on `v > 0`, so the 0 was a no-statement placeholder that read as if the penalty were modelled.

backfillRows.why: Print (heritage-270): 'However, your land Speed is reduced by 5 feet (to 20 feet for most seaweed leshies).' Nothing carried it: ancestries.leshy.speeds.land is 25, so the sheet printed 25. Reader derive.ts:4761.
Drops the `land: 0` placeholder that derive.ts:4726 discards anyway (`v > 0`), so the record no longer looks as if it states a land Speed. Swim 20 is print and is kept.

findings.note: Two-stage shape copied from heritages/budding-speaker-centaur (choice.flag 'speakerTradition' + spellFilter.traditionFromChoiceFlag) — a heritage, not just a feat, so the lane is proven on this record type. choiceFlagAnswer (build.ts:1749) explicitly searches `heritage:${build.heritageId}`; narrowSpellFilter (build.ts:1728) narrows the pool to the answer, and spellChoice.ts:54 then stamps that single tradition on the innate spell. effectChoices row SUPERSEDES the existing one (same block plus traditionFromChoiceFlag).

The tradition was never asked, so the innate spell fell back to the SPELL's own first tradition. Reader choiceFlagAnswer build.ts:1749 (`heritage:` key); precedent budding-speaker-centaur.

findings.note: Enumerated with node -e over public/core.json: the gnome ancestry feats carrying primal innateSpells rows are exactly FIVE — first-world-adept, homeward-bound, scarlet-strands, arboreal-conversationalist, kijimuna-whistle. (feats/first-world-magic ships no innateSpells at all, so it has no row to retune; that stub is out of batch.) Each row is a full-array replacement that SUPERSEDES the existing effect-backfill innateSpells row for that feat. ⚠ READER CAVEAT: asGranted/traditionFromFlag at build.ts:7012 loops FEATS ONLY (`for (const fc of feats) if (content.feats[fc.featId]?.choice?.flag === flag)`), so a flag asked by a HERITAGE resolves to undefined and these rows are inert until it is widened to choiceFlagAnswer — engine agent 1's half. Inert, never wrong: with no answer the tradition stays primal, exactly as today.

The two spellId rows are read by the static loop at src/rules/build.ts:5945-5957 (`for (const rec of ownedRecords) for (const n of rec?.spellNotes ?? [])`), which includes the heritage (build.ts:5874) and needs only a spellId. pushSpellNote keys by spell, so each note renders on the cantrip the player actually chose.

Cast from Makari Lizardfolk, this cantrip loses the manipulate trait — you cast purely by roaring and flaring your trunk.
Makari Lizardfolk: the tradition of this spell is divine instead of its normal tradition (usually primal).

backfillRows.why: Print (heritage-378): 'When you cast this cantrip, it loses the manipulate trait, as you cast purely by roaring and flaring your trunk' AND 'The tradition of any spells or magical abilities you gain from a lizardfolk heritage or ancestry feat is divine instead of its normal tradition.' Neither reached anything. Static reader build.ts:5945 for the two spellId rows; fromAncestrySpells reader build.ts:6005.

findings.note: The row lives on the MERGED spellNotes value above (one record + one field = one row). ⚠ READER CAVEAT: the fromAncestrySpells pass at build.ts:6003-6005 scans FEATS only (`wantsAncestrySpellNote = feats.map(...)`), so the heritage's row is inert until engine agent 1 widens that scan to the heritage record. Second, smaller caveat for the settle: that pass drops cantrips ('non-cantrip' is Ancestral Blood Magic's wording, not Makari's), so a cantrip gained from a lizardfolk ancestry feat will not carry the divine note even once the scan is widened.

Full-array replacement on the ACTION, not the heritage — the heritage's grantsActions:['tail-toxin'] is already correct. kobold and poison are kept per the proposal (the PC2 inline block prints only manipulate, but dropping the two legacy traits is not something print asks for).

backfillRows.why: Print (the PC2 block Venomtail Kobold grants, heritage-339): '**Tail Toxin** ⬻ (manipulate)'. Our record is the legacy APG printing with traits [kobold, poison] and no manipulate, so the trait line contradicts the text the heritage hands over.

findings.note: ⚠ THE DELETE IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE. scripts/lib/apply-backfill.mjs:56 bails with `if (!entry || !fix.field) continue;` and value:null only ever does `delete target[fix.field]` — there is no record-delete arm, so a {category:'classFeatures',id:'nudging-whisper',value:null} row would be a SILENT no-op. Reference check done first and clean: grep of src/ finds zero hits for the id (only scripts/apply-import-damaged-text.mjs:312, which targets the ACTIONS copy), no class feature table lists it, and a full core.json sweep of every other collection found no reference. So the twin is genuinely unreachable — ownedFeatureIds only ever yields class-listed features — and the only live harm is the damaged prose disagreeing with the actions copy in search/export. Shipping the finding's own stated fallback ('If it is kept instead, apply the same Confabulator repair'); the record deletion is listed under DATA STILL NEEDED. ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-03: the description-repair fallback is dropped; the record is DELETED outright via the new delete:true overlay arm (scripts/lib/apply-backfill.mjs).

grantsCreatureTraits reader: build.ts:5464 / creatureTraitsOf derive.ts:2831, used by 24 sibling heritages (fey-touched-gnome, undine, respite-of-loam-and-leaf). removesCreatureTraits has NO reader today — engine agent 2's subtractive pass in creatureTraitsOf — so it is authored here and is inert (never wrong) until that lands; without it the sheet would read 'leshy, plant, fungus', which print flatly denies.

backfillRows.why: Print (heritage-265): 'You lose the plant trait and gain the fungus trait.' A sweep of every collection in core.json found ZERO records granting a fungus creature trait. Reader derive.ts:2831.

Same printed clause, the losing half: ancestries.leshy.traits is ['leshy','plant'] and creatureTraitsOf is add-only, so shipping the fungus grant alone makes the Details tab read 'leshy, plant, fungus'. Field has no reader yet (engine agent 2).

findings.note: Description repair on the granted ACTION; the heritage's grantsActions:['wicked-thorns'] is already correct. SUPERSEDES the existing actions/wicked-thorns description row. Value mirrors public/ast/actions.json, which has the sentence intact — including print's own inconsistency ('1d4 persistent bleed damage' in the first mention, 'persistent piercing damage' in the second). Mirroring print, not reconciling it.

backfillRows.value:
**Trigger** You're hit with an unarmed Strike or a Strike with a non-reach melee weapon.

**Frequency** once per day

---

Several of your thorns break off and hook into your attacker's body. You deal 1d8 piercing damage to the triggering creature. It attempts a basic Reflex save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC. On a critical failure, the creature also takes 1d4 persistent bleed damage as your thorns embed in its flesh.

At 3rd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, this damage increases by 1d8, and the persistent piercing damage increases by 1.
backfillRows.why: Print (action-1449): 'You deal 1d8 piercing damage to the triggering creature' and '…the persistent piercing damage increases by 1.' The shipped fallback read 'You deal damage' (die and type deleted by the importer) and 'persistent bleed damage increases by 1'.

findings.note: DATA HALF ONLY. SUPERSEDES the existing unarmedTraits row — `remove:['nonlethal']` is dropped, `match` and `setDie` are kept verbatim. Print waives a PENALTY; it never removes the trait. derive.ts:4530 filtered 'nonlethal' out of FIST_PROFILE.traits, so the Strike row's trait line contradicted print — and WG's own item 18256 keeps Nonlethal.

findings.note: HALF 1 ONLY. findings.note: feats/halfling-luck VERIFIED present. The field has NO reader today — the eligibility filter that greys it out in the ancestry-feat picker is engine agent 1's — so this row is inert until that lands, and inert is not wrong (the picker behaves exactly as it does now).

Nothing on either side stopped the picker offering an illegal feat; a repo-wide grep for forbidsFeats/excludesFeats/cannotTake returns zero hits, so this is a new field awaiting its reader.

findings.note: Shaped exactly as the proposal specifies, reusing the vocabulary of the existing classFeature `skillProgression` lane (types.ts:1255, read at build.ts:5432-5438) but pointed at the record's OWN effectChoices answer, because print says 'that skill' — the same one the trained pick chose, not a second free choice like WG's shape. Reader is engine agent 1's (resolve build.effectChoices['ancient-ash:skill'], then maxRank the step). effectChoices is untouched, so no collision with the existing effectChoices row.

backfillRows.why: Print (heritage-207): 'You become trained in one skill of your choice. At 5th level, you become an expert in that skill.' The effectChoices grant is a flat 'trained' forever — applyAlwaysOn (build.ts:5452) has no level term, and the only level-stepped skill lane reads content.classFeatures only. maxRank semantics so a spent skill increase is never undone.
